newsitem.title: CHINA: China concedes that U.S. trade gap widening.
newsitem.headline: China concedes that U.S. trade gap widening.

text.p: China said on Friday its U.S. trade surplus jumped 22.5 percent in 1996 to $10.54 billion -- a figure that, despite its growth, was still billions of dollars less than Washington calculates.
A special customs report cited in the official China Daily said China's total trade with the United States rose 4.9 percent in 1996 to reach $42.84 billion against $40.83 billion in 1995.
China's exports to the United States rose 7.9 percent in 1996 to $26.69 billion, while U.S. imports rose just 0.2 percent to $16.15 billion, the report said.
The United States, which includes Chinese-made goods transshipped through Hong Kong in its trade figures, says the Chinese surplus was about $38.9 billion in 1996 against $34 billion in 1995.
The China Daily said the special customs report was released to coincide with Friday's 25th anniversary of the 1972 Shanghai Communique which opened relations between the two countries.

The report said the United States had replaced Hong Kong as China's second largest trade partner after Japan, and that processed goods such as shoes, toys and clothing accounted for 95 percent of its exports to the United States.
